prompt: The Ottoman Empire after the Young Turk Revolution, 1908
title: Journal of the Sublime Porte, 1908 to 1909
description: The Sultan named you Grand Vizier on 5 August 1908, twelve days after the Young Turk Revolution forced him to restore the Constitution of 1876. You lead the first constitutional cabinet.

sources.title: General Assembly of the Ottoman Empire

grounding: Grounded in the record of the Second Constitutional Era: the 1908 Ottoman general election results, the restored 1876 constitution, and Wikidata dates for Grand Viziers.

fall.what: Kâmil Pasha was forced out by a vote of no confidence in the Chamber of Deputies after replacing the Ministers of War and Navy without consulting the CUP; Hüseyin Hilmi Pasha succeeded him.

factions.name: Turkish deputies
factions.ideology: 147 of 275 seats, the Unionist core. They want a centralised state and Unionist ministers.

face.name: Rıfat Bey
face.role: Deputy for Konya, an invented voice

glance.strike: Votes the cabinet out on a motion of no confidence, on the Central Committee's word.

factions.name: Arab deputies
factions.ideology: 60 of 275 seats, many independent notables. They want Arabic in provincial offices and posts for their men.

face.name: Nadim Bey
face.role: Deputy for Beirut, an invented voice

glance.strike: Crosses to the Unionist benches on the next vote of confidence.

factions.name: Albanian deputies
factions.ideology: 27 of 275 seats. They want Albanian schools, local autonomy and no disarmament of the highlands.

face.name: Rexhep Bey
face.role: Deputy for Elbasan, an invented voice

glance.strike: Walks out of the Chamber and sends word to the highlands to keep their rifles.

factions.name: Greek deputies
factions.ideology: 26 of 275 seats. They want Patriarchate privileges, Greek schools and relief from conscription.

face.name: Konstantinos Efendi
face.role: Deputy for Smyrna, an invented voice

glance.strike: Votes with the Unionists and asks the Ecumenical Patriarchate to protest among the Powers.

factions.name: Armenian deputies
factions.ideology: 14 of 275 seats, Dashnak allies of the Unionists. They want seized eastern lands returned and Kurdish raids stopped.

face.name: Garabed Efendi
face.role: Deputy for Van, an invented voice

glance.strike: Its 14 deputies vote with the Turkish deputies against the cabinet and carry the land question to the Central Committee.

factions.name: Slav deputies
factions.ideology: 10 of 275 seats from Macedonia. They want Exarchist and Serb churches kept and village reprisals ended.

face.name: Todor Efendi
face.role: Deputy for Monastir, an invented voice

glance.strike: Its 10 deputies walk out of the Chamber of Deputies and take reports of reprisals to the foreign consuls in Salonica.

factions.name: Jewish deputies
factions.ideology: 4 of 275 seats, Ottomanist and close to Salonica. They want civic equality and stable trade.

face.name: Avram Efendi
face.role: Deputy for Salonica, an invented voice

glance.strike: Its 4 deputies side with the Salonica Unionists and vote against the cabinet on the next vote of confidence.

factions.name: Liberty Party
factions.ideology: Prince Sabahaddin's anglophile liberals, your allies. They want decentralisation and a cabinet free of the Committee.

face.name: Prince Sabahaddin
face.role: Founder of the Liberty Party, Constantinople

glance.strike: Prince Sabahaddin withdraws the party's support and calls the cabinet the Committee's servant in the Constantinople press.

blocs.name: Muslim peasants of Anatolia
blocs.description: Tithe-paying villagers who fill the conscript rolls and judge the constitution by the tax collector's visit.

blocs.name: Porters and boatmen of the ports
blocs.description: Dock guilds of Constantinople and Salonica who refuse to unload Austro-Hungarian cargo and want steady wages.

blocs.name: Christian merchants of the ports
blocs.description: Greek and Armenian traders of Smyrna, Galata and Salonica who want stable trade and fear Muslim-led conscription.

blocs.name: Ulema and religious students
blocs.description: Clergy and medrese students who distrust secular equality and look to the Sultan as Caliph.

blocs.name: Provincial notables and landowners
blocs.description: Beys, sheikhs and tax farmers of Syria, Iraq and Albania who want posts, land titles and a light hand from the Porte.

patrons.name: Unionist officers of the Third Army
Kurdish tribal chiefs of the east

members.name: Ahmed Rıza Bey
members.bio: From Monastir, he taught at a Salonica school before joining the Young Turk opposition. He wants the 1876 constitution enforced by a central government.
members.tell: He taps the constitution with two fingers before every vote.

glance.strike: He publishes a charge against the cabinet and calls Unionist deputies into opposition.

members.name: Mehmed Talat Bey
members.bio: From Edirne, he worked as a railway clerk before entering the Committee of Union and Progress. He wants Arab provinces to receive posts without weakening the Porte.
members.tell: He counts provincial appointments on the margin of his newspaper.

glance.strike: He trades his bloc's votes to a rival cabinet and opens talks with Arab notables.

members.name: İsmail Hakkı Bey
members.bio: From Van, he was a gendarmerie clerk who moved through eastern barracks before election. He wants a disciplined army and Ottoman control of the frontier.
members.tell: He keeps a folded military return beside his voting book.

glance.strike: He backs an army petition and withdraws Albanian deputies from the chamber.

members.name: Hüseyin Cahid Bey
members.bio: From Constantinople, he edited Tanin before taking the seat. He wants public debate under the constitution and a cabinet checked by the chamber.
members.tell: He writes objections in a black notebook while ministers speak.

glance.strike: He turns Tanin against the cabinet and demands a vote of no confidence.

members.name: Halil Menteşe Bey
members.bio: From Smyrna, he ran a customs office and later organised constitutional clubs in Monastir. He wants seized Armenian land returned through courts.
members.tell: He asks for the registry number of every eastern land file.

glance.strike: He joins Armenian deputies in a public indictment of the ministers.

members.name: Nâzım Pasha
members.bio: From Baghdad, he was a provincial judge before entering politics. He wants the Sultan's authority preserved and religious courts protected from abrupt reform.
members.tell: He kisses his signet before recording each division.

glance.strike: He petitions the Sultan and urges the ulema to denounce the ministry.

members.name: Hasan Fehmi Bey
members.bio: From Jeddah, he owned a grain warehouse and joined the Ottomanist club of Beirut. He wants cheap bread and equal trade rules for the provinces.
members.tell: He carries a loaf into committee when grain prices rise.

glance.strike: He leads a bread petition and withholds his bloc from every finance vote.

members.name: Rıza Tevfik Bey
members.bio: From Ioannina, he taught philosophy and wrote poems before joining Prince Sabahaddin's circle. He wants local government and a cabinet free of the Committee.
members.tell: He quotes Rousseau when a minister asks for emergency powers.

glance.strike: He calls a Liberty Party conference and demands the cabinet's resignation.

members.name: Mustafa Asım Bey
members.bio: From Konya, he was a village tax assessor before winning a seat in the first constitutional election. He wants lower levies for cultivators.
members.tell: He rubs tax dust from his cuffs before speaking about villages.

glance.strike: He returns to Anatolia and organises petitions against the cabinet's tax and draft orders.

members.name: Mehmed Şerif Bey
members.bio: From Damascus, he served as a court translator and provincial secretary. He wants Arabic offices recognised while the imperial treasury stays united.
members.tell: He corrects every Arabic place name in the printed minutes.

glance.strike: He forms an Arab caucus and blocks the cabinet's provincial legislation.

members.name: Süleyman Askerî Bey
members.bio: From Mosul, he was a cavalry supply contractor before entering Unionist politics. He wants eastern roads and paid troops under direct state control.
members.tell: He checks a pocket map whenever the chamber debates a frontier province.

glance.strike: He carries a military complaint to the Third Army and withdraws support from the ministry.

members.name: Musa Kâzım Efendi
members.bio: From Constantinople, he ran a printing shop near the Fatih district. He wants the chamber to restrain ministers without ending the Sultan's religious authority.
members.tell: He folds ministerial speeches into paper boats during long sittings.

glance.strike: He joins a palace delegation and votes against the cabinet's confidence.

members.name: Abdülkadir Kemali Bey
members.bio: From Salonica, he was a railway surveyor and club organiser before election. He wants Macedonian security with legal protection for Armenian villages.
members.tell: He marks village names in red on railway survey sheets.

glance.strike: He exposes military failures in committee and votes with the opposition.

members.name: Cemal Azmi Bey
members.bio: From Basra, he was a medrese lecturer and judge's aide. He wants Islamic authority kept inside the restored constitution and fears sudden secular legislation.
members.tell: He recites a short prayer before signing a committee report.

glance.strike: He appeals to the şeyhülislam and brings religious students into the capital.

members.name: Ali Fethi Bey
members.bio: From Jerusalem, he was an infantry captain who later worked in the Ottoman diplomatic service. He wants orderly government and a professional army under parliament.
members.tell: He straightens his old service ribbon before military debates.

glance.strike: He signs a officers' memorandum and joins a parliamentary move against the minister.

members.name: Mehmed Cavid Bey
members.bio: From Ioannina, he studied finance in Paris and ran a bank in Salonica. He wants balanced budgets and European credit without foreign control of policy.
members.tell: He calculates each proposal in francs on the back of a voting slip.

glance.strike: He resigns from the finance committee and urges bankers to refuse cabinet credit.

members.name: Şükrü Kaya Bey
members.bio: From Aleppo, he was a school inspector and newspaper writer. He wants an elected chamber with Arabic education and fewer police arrests.
members.tell: He asks witnesses to name the police officer who ordered an arrest.

glance.strike: He publishes arrest lists and brings an Arab delegation before the chamber.

members.name: Yusuf Hikmet Bey
members.bio: From Hama, he inherited an estate and served on a provincial grain board. He wants local councils to protect landowners from officials and tax farmers.
members.tell: He rolls a silver seal across the desk while bargaining over a province.

glance.strike: He withholds Syrian votes and funds a provincial delegation to the Palace.

members.name: Said Halim Pasha
members.bio: From Alexandria, he studied law and wrote constitutional essays in Paris. He wants an Ottoman charter with provincial rights and a cabinet under law.
members.tell: He underlines the same constitutional clause in every draft.

glance.strike: He drafts a censure motion and signs a Liberty Party appeal.

members.name: Hüseyin Hilmi Bey
members.bio: From Erzurum, he was a provincial governor's secretary during the Hamidian years. He wants order in the capital and protection for Armenian villages.
members.tell: He keeps a list of eastern petitions tied with blue thread.

glance.strike: He reads the petitions aloud and votes against any cabinet that refuses an inquiry.

members.name: Midhat Şükrü Bey
members.bio: From Monastir, he worked as a post clerk and carried messages for the Young Turks. He wants Unionist ministers and a single state administration.
members.tell: He arrives before the doors open and counts Unionist seats.

glance.strike: He rallies the Central Committee's deputies and forces a ministerial replacement.

members.name: Mehmed Nazım Bey
members.bio: From Baghdad, he was a date merchant who financed a local Ottomanist newspaper. He wants provincial spending and relief from conscription's burden.
members.tell: He compares army draft lists with the names of market apprentices.

glance.strike: He leads an Iraqi petition and votes down the next military appropriation.

members.name: Mustafa Zihni Bey
members.bio: From Medina, he was a caravan broker and municipal treasurer. He wants roads, paid garrisons and a bargain with tribal chiefs rather than forced disarmament.
members.tell: He places a camel-hair cord beside each provincial estimate.

glance.strike: He brokers a provincial bloc and refuses the cabinet's emergency decree.

members.name: Ahmet Muhtar Bey
members.bio: From Shkodër, he was a schoolmaster and municipal clerk before election. He wants Albanian schools and local authority within the empire.
members.tell: He switches between Albanian and Ottoman Turkish when reading a petition.

glance.strike: He calls Albanian deputies together and blocks the ministry's disarmament bill.

members.name: Süleyman Sırrı Bey
members.bio: From Ankara, he was a grain broker and union organiser in the railway town. He wants cheap bread, fair taxes and a state that pays its soldiers.
members.tell: He asks the chamber usher for the day's bread price before voting.

glance.strike: He joins a provincial protest and refuses to defend the cabinet in his district.

members.name: Osman Nuri Bey
members.bio: From Damascus, he was a customs clerk and provincial secretary. He entered politics through the Beirut reform clubs. He wants Arabic in Syrian offices and a cabinet loyal to the Sultan.
members.tell: He taps his seal twice before agreeing to a government motion.

glance.strike: He withdraws Arab support and urges Damascus notables to refuse Porte orders.

members.name: İbrahim Temo Bey
members.bio: From Shkodra, he was a physician who joined the Young Turk movement in Geneva. He wants Albanian schools under a constitutional state, not rule by palace decree.
members.tell: He corrects Ottoman Turkish terms in every committee report.

glance.strike: He publishes a constitutional appeal and joins the Albanian opposition.

members.name: İsmail Kemal Bey
members.bio: From Vlorë, he was a lawyer, merchant and member of the Ottoman reform clubs. He wants a cabinet drawn from the chamber and provincial councils with real powers.
members.tell: He leaves the chamber during speeches and returns with two new promises.

glance.strike: He brokers a vote of no confidence with the Liberty Party.

members.name: Esad Toptani Bey
members.bio: From Tirana, he was a gendarmerie officer and landholder in Macedonia. He wants cheap bread, strong order and Albanian recruits kept near their homes.
members.tell: He points at the public gallery whenever he mentions hungry soldiers.

glance.strike: He rallies Muslim deputies against the cabinet and calls for martial law.

members.name: Bajram Curri Bey
members.bio: From Peja, he was a highland landowner and rifle broker before entering the chamber. He wants roads, customs posts and bargains that leave Albanian chiefs armed.
members.tell: He folds every government paper into a narrow strip before reading it.

glance.strike: He sends letters to Iraqi and Albanian patrons and blocks the budget.

members.name: Haxhi Zeka Bey
members.bio: From Peja, he was a merchant and commander in the League of Peja. He wants Albanian schools and local rule without disarmament by Constantinople.
members.tell: He keeps a highland dagger on the desk during every military debate.

glance.strike: He leaves the chamber and calls the highland chiefs to resist the Porte.

members.name: Aşir Efendi
members.bio: From Elbasan, he was a school inspector and clerk in the Ministry of Education. He wants a lawful Albanian school system under an elected constitutional government.
members.tell: He counts the chamber doors before each division.

glance.strike: He files a constitutional protest and joins the Liberty Party caucus.

members.name: Mehmed Pashë Dibra
members.bio: From Dibra, he was a tax farmer and grain dealer in Anatolia. He wants lower village dues and a government that pays soldiers before ordering new campaigns.
members.tell: He asks the clerk for the grain price before voting on any bill.

glance.strike: He withholds his vote and calls Anatolian deputies into a budget bloc.

members.name: Şemsi Pasha
members.bio: From Ioannina, he was a provincial judge and tobacco broker. He wants the Porte to keep Albanian loyalties through posts and taxes, not disarmament.
members.tell: He rubs his thumb across a gold signet when a minister refuses a bargain.

glance.strike: He carries his faction's votes to the rival cabinet and demands a governorship.

members.name: Abdullah Cevdet Bey
members.bio: From Diyarbakır, he was a physician and journalist who joined the Young Turk circles. He wants secular law, a free press and provincial education for Kurds and Arabs.
members.tell: He writes medical notes in the margin of every military report.

glance.strike: He prints an attack on the ministry and works with the Liberty Party.

members.name: Fazıl Küçük Bey
members.bio: From Famagusta, he was a schoolmaster and newspaper editor in Constantinople. He wants equal civic law and a navy budget that protects Ottoman ports.
members.tell: He draws a small ship beside every naval appropriation.

glance.strike: He denounces the cabinet in print and votes with the liberal opposition.

members.name: Abd al-Hamid al-Zahrawi
members.bio: From Hama, he was a lawyer and editor of al-Mufid. He wants Arabic administration and an Ottoman constitution enforced against palace and committee rule.
members.tell: He places Arabic petitions on top of every Turkish memorandum.

glance.strike: He forms an Arab caucus and refuses confidence in the grand vizier.

members.name: Shukri al-Asali
members.bio: From Damascus, he was a judge and railway lawyer. He wants elected control of ministers and Arabic rights within one Ottoman state.
members.tell: He reads the same constitutional clause aloud until ministers answer it.

glance.strike: He demands a chamber inquiry and signs the opposition's censure motion.

members.name: Rafiq al-Azm
members.bio: From Damascus, he was a silk merchant and municipal notable. He wants order in the provinces, safe caravans and gradual Arabic administrative reform.
members.tell: He keeps a merchant's ledger open beside the voting list.

glance.strike: He closes his business network to the cabinet and shifts his votes to Prince Sabahaddin.

members.name: Abd al-Ghani al-Uraysi
members.bio: From Beirut, he was a printer and newspaper owner. He wants an Arab press free from the censor and a cabinet checked by elected deputies.
members.tell: He tears censor marks from proofs in full view of the ministers.

glance.strike: He prints the ministry's secret orders and backs a vote of censure.

members.name: Sulayman al-Bustani
members.bio: From Beirut, he was a civil engineer and shipping investor. He wants roads, port works and Arabic schools funded through regular budgets.
members.tell: He measures the chamber bench with a ruler during budget debates.

glance.strike: He leads Lebanese deputies out and refuses the government's financial bill.

members.name: Rashid Rida
members.bio: From Tripoli, Syria, he was a printer, editor and Islamic reform writer. He wants Muslim education and a constitution guarded from European control.
members.tell: He quotes a Quranic verse before answering a Unionist whip.

glance.strike: He appeals to the ulema and attacks the cabinet as an agent of Britain.

members.name: Hafiz al-Said
members.bio: From Mosul, he was a provincial clerk and grain assessor. He wants reliable tax collection, paid troops and offices open to Arab officials.
members.tell: He checks the treasury figures against a small notebook from Mosul.

glance.strike: He withholds the Mosul vote and demands the minister's resignation.

members.name: Jamil al-Midfai
members.bio: From Baghdad, he was a cavalry officer and provincial administrator. He wants an orderly army and Arab officers promoted without weakening the empire.
members.tell: He stands whenever a general enters the chamber.

glance.strike: He persuades officers to refuse the ministry's preferred appointment.

members.name: Tawfiq al-Suwaidi
members.bio: From Baghdad, he was a lawyer and municipal councillor. He wants elected provincial councils and courts that restrain governors.
members.tell: He folds his spectacles before every vote on provincial law.

glance.strike: He joins a formal opposition bloc and brings Baghdad petitions before the chamber.

members.name: Ali Rida al-Rikabi
members.bio: From Damascus, he was an artillery officer and railway administrator. He wants a disciplined ministry and Arab advancement inside a central Ottoman army.
members.tell: He marks army bills with red pencil and refuses oral assurances.

glance.strike: He pressures the officer caucus to abandon the cabinet in the next division.

members.name: Sami Faruqi Pasha
members.bio: From Aleppo, he was a cavalry commander and provincial landholder. He wants cheap bread and government posts for Arab soldiers and notables.
members.tell: He slaps the table whenever a minister mentions new taxes.

glance.strike: He leads Arab deputies against the ministry and calls for a new cabinet.

members.name: Abd al-Muhsin al-Sa'dun
members.bio: From Baghdad, he was a land surveyor and provincial administrator. He wants a strong central state that pays its army and curbs local tax farmers.
members.tell: He carries a rolled map and points to each province under debate.

glance.strike: He votes with the Unionist officers and seeks a ministry post to enforce the budget.

members.name: Muhammad al-Mahdi al-Istambuli
members.bio: From Jerusalem, he was a court clerk and waqf administrator. He wants Arabic schools, protected endowments and a constitution respected in Palestine.
members.tell: He recites the names of Jerusalem waqfs before discussing any land bill.

glance.strike: He gathers Jerusalem petitions and votes against the cabinet's provincial bill.

members.name: Yusuf al-Khalidi
members.bio: From Jerusalem, he was a mayor, judge and municipal reformer. He wants elected councils, Arabic administration and secure trade through the empire.
members.tell: He asks which municipality will pay before supporting every public work.

glance.strike: He joins Prince Sabahaddin's liberals and helps bring down the ministry.

members.name: Naji al-Suwaidi
members.bio: From Baghdad, he was a commercial lawyer and Ottoman administrator before entering the chamber. He wants Iraqi notables to control provincial offices.
members.tell: He taps his signet against the desk before naming his price.

glance.strike: He joins Arab deputies and blocks the ministry's provincial bills.

members.name: Salim al-Bakri
members.bio: From Damascus, he was a school inspector and newspaper editor before the seat. He wants the constitution protected under Unionist rule.
members.tell: He rises before the whip calls his name and salutes the ministry bench.

glance.strike: He denounces the ruler in Damascus and calls for Unionist discipline.

members.name: Mikail Aslanian
members.bio: From Erzurum, he was a railway surveyor and provincial clerk before election. He wants Armenian villages protected from Kurdish raids by law.
members.tell: He keeps a folded map of the eastern provinces under his papers.

glance.strike: He withdraws Armenian votes and presses the army command for eastern protection.

members.name: Krikor Zohrab
members.bio: From Constantinople, he was a barrister and novelist before the seat. He wants constitutional courts to protect Armenians and Muslims alike.
members.tell: He quotes a court ruling before answering any minister.

glance.strike: He leads a legal bloc against the cabinet and publishes its abuses.

members.name: Vartkes Serengülian
members.bio: From Van, he was a teacher, printer and Hunchak organiser before the seat. He wants eastern land claims settled through a chamber commission.
members.tell: He marks every speech with a red pencil in the margin of the minutes.

glance.strike: He joins the Armenian opposition and turns every committee hearing against the ministry.

members.name: Aram Manukian
members.bio: From Muş, he was a village doctor and Dashnak courier before election. He wants Armenian schools reopened under Ottoman law.
members.tell: He carries a doctor's black bag into every provincial committee meeting.

glance.strike: He refuses the budget and organizes Armenian deputies around relief petitions.

members.name: Hovhannes Bozabalian
members.bio: From Sivas, he was a grain dealer who led a market petition before election. He wants cheaper bread and honest tax collection.
members.tell: He brings a sack of village grain to the chamber lobby.

glance.strike: He rallies Anatolian deputies and refuses supply votes.

members.name: Garabed Pastırmacıyan
members.bio: From Erzurum, he was an engineer, physician and fedayi commander before the seat. He wants an eastern reform inspectorate with armed authority.
members.tell: He measures the chamber benches with a surveyor's rule.

glance.strike: He breaks with the Unionists and demands an armed reform mission in the east.

members.name: Hagop Babikian
members.bio: From Bursa, he was a silk merchant and Armenian community trustee before election. He wants commercial courts free from palace interference.
members.tell: He folds contracts into precise squares while ministers speak.

glance.strike: He moves the merchant bloc to withhold loans and committee support.

members.name: Artin Boshgezenian
members.bio: From Kayseri, he was a provincial judge and court registrar before the seat. He wants one civil law for every Ottoman subject.
members.tell: He corrects the clerk's legal terms without looking up.

glance.strike: He files a constitutional motion and refuses every emergency decree.

members.name: Emanuel Karasu
members.bio: From Salonica, he was a lawyer and Young Turk organiser before election. He wants equal civic rights enforced by a strong parliament.
members.tell: He writes names in Ladino before switching to Ottoman Turkish.

glance.strike: He coordinates Salonica deputies and demands the cabinet answer in public.

members.name: Nissim Mazliah
members.bio: From Salonica, he was a schoolmaster and Ladino newspaper columnist before the seat. He wants Jewish schools and trade protected by statute.
members.tell: He reads every dispatch aloud in Ladino before voting.

glance.strike: He turns the Salonica Jewish association against the ministry's candidates.

members.name: David Fresco
members.bio: From Smyrna, he was a tobacco broker and communal treasurer before election. He wants stable customs rates and no port blockade.
members.tell: He checks the day's customs prices on a cigarette paper.

glance.strike: He joins port merchants and blocks customs legislation.

members.name: Mois Cohen
members.bio: From Adrianople, he was a railway contractor and municipal councillor before the seat. He wants the Oriental Railway kept in Ottoman hands.
members.tell: He carries a railway timetable and folds it at every disputed line.

glance.strike: He withholds transport votes and funds a commercial challenge to the cabinet.

members.name: Emmanuel Emmanuelidis
members.bio: From Chios, he was a doctor at the Greek hospital in Smyrna before election. He wants Greek schools and conscription exemptions restored.
members.tell: He checks his pocket watch whenever conscription enters debate.

glance.strike: He joins Greek deputies in refusing military appropriations.

members.name: Georgios Kambouroglou
members.bio: From Constantinople, he was a customs lawyer and municipal clerk before the seat. He wants the Patriarchate's courts and schools left intact.
members.tell: He underlines every reference to the Patriarchate in blue ink.

glance.strike: He organizes a Greek procedural bloc and stalls the chamber's agenda.

members.name: Alexandros Pallis
members.bio: From Salonica, he was a philologist and Greek newspaper editor before election. He wants language rights written into the constitution.
members.tell: He answers Turkish speeches with a Greek quotation from Herodotus.

glance.strike: He publishes a Greek appeal and votes against every Unionist ministry.

members.name: Konstantinos Zografos
members.bio: From Trebizond, he was a shipping agent and port councillor before election. He wants coastal trade spared from military requisition.
members.tell: He rubs salt from his cuffs before speaking on naval supply.

glance.strike: He takes the coastal deputies out of the chamber and breaks the supply vote.

members.name: Nikolaos Vamvakaris
members.bio: From Smyrna, he was a dock foreman and union treasurer before the seat. He wants port wages paid on time and food prices checked.
members.tell: He counts coins on the rail before every labor speech.

glance.strike: He calls port workers into the streets and votes against the cabinet.

members.name: Sotirios Goudas
members.bio: From Constantinople, he was a grain importer and Greek communal trustee before election. He wants cheap flour and predictable customs.
members.tell: He asks the clerk for flour prices before he asks about the bill.

glance.strike: He uses merchant credit to isolate the ministry from its suppliers.

members.name: Pavle Šterijov
members.bio: From Monastir, he was a railway telegraphist and reserve officer before election. He wants Macedonia held by the constitution and the army.
members.tell: He checks the telegraph clock before each Macedonian vote.

glance.strike: He backs the Third Army officers and forces a confidence vote.

members.name: Dimitar Vlahov
members.bio: From Salonica, he was a Bulgarian-language teacher and railway union organizer before election. He wants Exarchist schools and an end to village reprisals.
members.tell: He keeps a Bulgarian primer open beside the chamber register.

glance.strike: He joins the Slav bloc and makes the Macedonian budget impossible to pass.

citizens.name: Mehmed Rauf
citizens.worldview: I want the tax collector to take less and the army to leave my sons at harvest.

citizens.name: Hüseyin Sırrı
citizens.worldview: I want the Porte to keep order without sending officials who know nothing of our villages.

citizens.name: İbrahim Naci
citizens.worldview: I want protection from raids and a fair court for every tribe.

citizens.name: Ahmed Şevket
citizens.worldview: I want bread to cost less and the new constitution to survive the palace.

citizens.name: Mustafa Fikri
citizens.worldview: I want the bands disarmed and local men spared from reprisals.

citizens.name: Halil Ziya
citizens.worldview: I want Baghdad to keep more revenue and Constantinople to appoint fewer strangers.

citizens.name: Ali Rıza
citizens.worldview: I want the Hejaz Railway paid for and the Sultan's authority kept in the holy cities.

citizens.name: Yusuf Cemal
citizens.worldview: I want Albanian schools and rifles kept in our homes against outside officials.

citizens.name: Osman Nuri
citizens.worldview: I want cheap bread and no new levy for ministers who live in Constantinople.

citizens.name: Süleyman Tevfik
citizens.worldview: I want local councils to settle taxes and schools without constant orders from the Porte.

citizens.name: Hasan Tahsin
citizens.worldview: I want the gendarmes to stop Kurdish raids and return land taken from Armenian villages.

citizens.name: Mahmud Celal
citizens.worldview: I want wages to rise with prices and the censors to leave our newspapers alone.

citizens.name: İsmail Hakkı
citizens.worldview: I want the bands pardoned when they lay down arms and the army to stop burning villages.

citizens.name: Abdülkadir Refik

citizens.worldview: The government must keep order without taking pasture or accepting every complaint against Kurdish families.

citizens.name: Mariam Deranian
citizens.worldview: Schools and courts must treat Armenian villagers as citizens under the constitution.

citizens.name: Siranush Kevorkian
citizens.worldview: The Porte must protect Christian schools and return land taken through corrupt provincial courts.

citizens.name: Eleni Papadopoulou
citizens.worldview: The government must keep conscription fair and protect Greek schools from local officials.

citizens.name: Despoina Vlastou
citizens.worldview: Trade needs stable taxes, and Greek communities need the Patriarchate's rights left intact.

citizens.name: Katerina Theodoraki
citizens.worldview: The Porte must stop arbitrary censorship and let merchants trade without palace favourites.

citizens.name: Yitzhak Ben-Ami
citizens.worldview: Civic equality and stable customs will keep Jewish merchants loyal to the empire.

citizens.name: Moshe Baruch
citizens.worldview: The government must protect trade and stop foreign debt claims from ruling every commercial decision.

citizens.name: Lazar Cohen
citizens.worldview: Bread must stay affordable, while the Porte keeps the ports open to lawful commerce.

citizens.name: Esther Mizrahi
citizens.worldview: The constitution must secure equal citizenship and remove palace privilege from commercial life.

citizens.name: Fatma Hanım
citizens.worldview: The Porte must end censorship and protect contracts from officials who serve the palace household.

starts.premise: 147 of 275 seats, the Unionist core. They want a centralised state and Unionist ministers.
60 of 275 seats, many independent notables. They want Arabic in provincial offices and posts for their men.
27 of 275 seats. They want Albanian schools, local autonomy and no disarmament of the highlands.
26 of 275 seats. They want Patriarchate privileges, Greek schools and relief from conscription.
14 of 275 seats, Dashnak allies of the Unionists. They want seized eastern lands returned and Kurdish raids stopped.
10 of 275 seats from Macedonia. They want Exarchist and Serb churches kept and village reprisals ended.
4 of 275 seats, Ottomanist and close to Salonica. They want civic equality and stable trade.
Prince Sabahaddin's anglophile liberals, your allies. They want decentralisation and a cabinet free of the Committee.

problems: The Central Committee in Salonica wants every cabinet choice put to it first, and Talaat Bey says so openly.
Alois Aehrenthal is preparing Vienna to annex Bosnia and Herzegovina, held under the Treaty of Berlin since 1878.
Ferdinand I is preparing to declare Bulgaria independent and to seize the Oriental Railway.
The Sultan and the Central Committee both claim the right to name the Ministers of War and Navy.
The Hunter battalions of the Constantinople garrison resent the Unionist officers who now command them.
Bulgarian, Greek and Serb bands still fight over the villages of Ottoman Macedonia.
The Cretans want union with the Kingdom of Greece, and Georgios Theotokis will not refuse them.
Workers in Constantinople are striking for wages that have not kept pace with prices since the famine of 1905.

deck.memory: He paid the dockers before he paid the state.
He sent grain before asking who would repay it.

deck.title_hint: A deputy's papers reach the press
deck.memory: He made a private file a public weapon.

stances: Give the post to his man
deck.memory: He kept one promise and lost a friend.
He survived by giving the army another master.

deck.title_hint: Trade falls at the Golden Horn
deck.memory: He chose between empty purses and angry soldiers.
He learned that a constitution can bind a palace.
He saved the coalition and stained its name.
He answered annexation with empty Austrian warehouses.
He borrowed abroad to keep the barracks quiet.

stances: Use his name, then refuse him
deck.memory: He turned a prince's blessing into a brief truce.

deck.title_hint: The press turns against the cabinet
deck.memory: He found that censorship could not restore trust.
He gained a vote by naming the language.
He spent a lucky month on old arrears.

deck.title_hint: The capital has a quiet week
deck.memory: For one week, no faction needed him.

deck.title_hint: The Palace stages a public prayer
deck.memory: He stood beside the Caliph and lost the reformers.
He learned who held the rifles.
He made secrecy a test of the new regime.

deck.title_hint: A Greek deputy seeks a bargain
deck.memory: He bought a vote and inherited a grievance.

deck.title_hint: The cabinet counts its final days
deck.memory: He left office with the chamber still divided.
The Young Turk Revolution forced Abdülhamid II to restore the constitution.
The Chamber of Deputies reopened under the restored constitution.
Ferdinand I declared Bulgaria independent while the Porte protested.
Alois Aehrenthal announced Austria-Hungary's annexation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
The Ottoman general election gave the Committee of Union and Progress the strongest bloc.
The Chamber of Deputies opened in Constantinople after the first constitutional election.
A mutiny in the capital could have brought the 31 March crisis forward.
Abdülhamid II could have dismissed the constitutional cabinet before the crisis of April 1909.
An early Balkan war could have ended constitutional politics before the Balkan Wars of 1912.

escalations.name: Tanin turns on the Porte
escalations.headline: Tanin prints a daily attack on your cabinet, and the Constantinople press follows its lead.

escalations.name: The Unionist bloc
escalations.headline: Unionist deputies can now carry 184 of 275 votes in the Chamber without you.

escalations.name: Trade falls away
escalations.headline: The boycott of Austrian goods and the loss of Bulgarian revenue cut the Porte's receipts by a quarter.

escalations.name: Hamidian files opened
escalations.headline: Spy reports from the old regime reach the press, and several name men in your cabinet.

escalations.name: Tempers in the Chamber
escalations.headline: Deputies shout down your ministers, and a draft law can be rejected on one bad sitting.

escalations.name: A Chamber without a majority
escalations.headline: No bloc can carry 138 of 275 votes, and every draft law needs a new bargain.

escalations.name: Every vote has a price
escalations.headline: Deputies ask posts, roads and pardons before each division, and the clerk's price rises each fortnight.

escalations.name: Public favour wavers
escalations.headline: The crowds that cheered the constitution in July now cheer whoever spoke to them last.

escalations.name: The treasury is empty
escalations.headline: Officers' and officials' salaries run three months behind, and the Ottoman Public Debt Administration holds the best revenues.

escalations.name: The Senate stalls
escalations.headline: The Senate, named by the Sultan, sits on your draft laws and sends them back amended.

escalations.name: Hilmi Pasha is ready
escalations.headline: The Central Committee lets it be known that Hüseyin Hilmi Pasha is ready to form a cabinet.

escalations.name: Empty benches
escalations.headline: Fewer than half of the 275 deputies attend, and draft laws wait for a quorum.

escalations.name: Deputies cross over
escalations.headline: Arab and Albanian deputies who voted with you in the autumn begin to vote with the Unionists.

escalations.name: Mass meetings in the capital
escalations.headline: Unionist speakers fill the squares of Constantinople and call for your resignation.

escalations.name: Too many alarms
escalations.headline: Bulgaria, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Crete have all been lost in one autumn, and the Chamber blames the Porte for each.

escalations.name: Cabinet secrets in Tanin
escalations.headline: Your cabinet's decisions appear in Tanin the morning after the ministers take them.

escalations.name: Mobilisation on the frontier
escalations.headline: Reserves are called up against Bulgaria, and the Army asks the Porte for credits it does not have.

escalations.name: Bread dearth
escalations.headline: The harvest fails in the Anatolian heartland, and the price of bread doubles in Constantinople.

escalations.name: The question of the throne
escalations.headline: Deputies and officers talk openly of deposing the Sultan and seating his brother, the heir.

escalations.name: The Powers press the Porte
escalations.headline: The ambassadors of the Powers present demands on Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria and Crete in a single week.

test.name: Vote of confidence in the Chamber of Deputies
test.win: You keep the votes of at least 138 of 275 deputies and remain Grand Vizier at the Sublime Porte.
test.lose: Fewer than 138 of 275 deputies stand by you, and the Central Committee puts Hüseyin Hilmi Pasha forward in your place.

endings.defeated: Voted out by the Chamber of Deputies
endings.lame_duck: Grand Vizier in name at the Porte
endings.impeached: Ministers sent for trial by the Chamber
endings.coup: The Third Army marches on Constantinople

pork.label: A road for the sanjak
pork.text: You pledge a road, a school or a telegraph line in the deputy's district, paid from the Porte's funds.

favor.label: A post at the Porte
favor.text: You name the deputy's kinsman or client to a governorship, a customs office or a ministry desk, and he votes with you on the next draft law.

threat.label: The Porte dossier
threat.text: You let the deputy know that the Hamidian spy reports on his past are in your chancery and can reach the Constantinople press.

ruler.role: Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire, head of the first constitutional cabinet at the Sublime Porte
ruler.removedBy: Sultan Abdul Hamid II can dismiss you by imperial decree, the Chamber of Deputies can vote you out by no confidence, and the Committee of Union and Progress can press both to do so.

briefing.situation: The Sultan named you Grand Vizier on 5 August 1908, twelve days after the Young Turk Revolution forced him to restore the Constitution of 1876. You lead the first constitutional cabinet. The Committee of Union and Progress made the revolution. It sits in Salonica and expects its Central Committee to be consulted. Austria-Hungary eyes Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the Principality of Bulgaria wants full independence. You want a cabinet that answers to the Sublime Porte and elections held under your hand.
briefing.room: Sultan Abdul Hamid II can dismiss you by imperial decree, and every draft law needs his sanction. The Central Committee holds no ministry, but its officers lead the Third Army and Tanin prints its line. This autumn's elections fill all 275 seats of the Chamber of Deputies. Once the Chamber sits, 138 of 275 votes can bring you down. The Turkish deputies, 147 of 275, follow the Committee.
briefing.you: You hold the imperial seal and the cabinet, and you preside over the Senate. You name ministers, draft laws and set the budget. The Ottoman Public Debt Administration collects key revenues first. Britain backs you. The Liberty Party of Prince Sabahaddin is your ally, with 1 of 275 seats once the Chamber sits. A vote of confidence asks the Chamber whether it still trusts your cabinet. If you lose it, you fall.
